units.text: INT. PYGMALION - CONTINUOUS
He takes the hat.
Handle it carefully, sir, please. I had to promise her not to burn it; but I had better put it in the oven for a while.
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: HIGGINS [putting it down hastily on the piano] Oh! thank you.
Well, what have you to say to me?
Am I in the way?
units.name: PICKERING

units.text: Not at all, sir. Mr. Higgins: will you please be very particular what you say before the girl?
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: HIGGINS [sternly] Of course.
I’m always particular about what I say.
Why do you say this to me?
PEARCE
units.name: MRS

units.text: unmoved.
No, sir: you’re not at all particular when you’ve mislaid anything or when you get a little impatient. Now it doesn’t matter before me: I’m used to it. But you really must not swear before the girl.
units.name: MRS

units.text: HIGGINS [indignantly] I swear! [Most emphatically] I never swear.
I detest the habit.
What the devil do you mean?
PEARCE
units.name: MRS

units.text: stolidly.
That’s what I mean, sir. You swear a great deal too much. I don’t mind your damning and blasting, and what the devil and where the devil and who the devil—
units.name: MRS

units.text: Really! Mrs. Pearce: this language from your lips!
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: PEARCE
units.name: MRS

units.text: not to be put off.

—but there is a certain word I must ask you not to use. The girl has just used it herself because the bath was too hot. It begins with the same letter as bath. She knows no better: she learnt it at her mother’s knee. But she must not hear it from your lips.
units.name: MRS

units.text: HIGGINS [loftily] I cannot charge myself with having ever uttered it, Mrs. Pearce. [She looks at him steadfastly.
He adds, hiding an uneasy conscience with a judicial air] Except perhaps in a moment of extreme and justifiable excitement.
Only this morning, sir, you applied it to your boots, to the butter, and to the brown bread.
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: Oh, that! Mere alliteration, Mrs. Pearce, natural to a poet.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Well, sir, whatever you choose to call it, I beg you not to let the girl hear you repeat it.
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: Oh, very well, very well. Is that all?
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: No, sir. We shall have to be very particular with this girl as to personal cleanliness.
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: Certainly. Quite right. Most important.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: I mean not to be slovenly about her dress or untidy in leaving things about.
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: HIGGINS [going to her solemnly] Just so.
I intended to call your attention to that [He passes on to Pickering, who is enjoying the conversation immensely].
It is these little things that matter, Pickering.
Take care of the pence and the pounds will take care of themselves is as true of personal habits as of money. [He comes to anchor on the hearthrug, with the air of a man in an unassailable position].

Yes, sir. Then might I ask you not to come down to breakfast in your dressing-gown, or at any rate not to use it as a napkin to the extent you do, sir. And if you would be so good as not to eat everything off the same plate, and to remember not to put the porridge saucepan out of your hand on the clean tablecloth, it would be a better example to the girl. You know you nearly choked yourself with a fishbone in the jam only last week.
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: HIGGINS [routed from the hearthrug and drifting back to the piano] I may do these things sometimes in absence of mind; but surely I don’t do them habitually. [Angrily] By the way: my dressing-gown smells most damnably of benzine.
No doubt it does, Mr. Higgins. But if you will wipe your fingers—
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: HIGGINS [yelling] Oh very well, very well: I’ll wipe them in my hair in future.
I hope you’re not offended, Mr. Higgins.
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: HIGGINS [shocked at finding himself thought capable of an unamiable sentiment] Not at all, not at all.
You’re quite right, Mrs. Pearce: I shall be particularly careful before the girl.
Is that all?
No, sir. Might she use some of those Japanese dresses you brought from abroad? I really can’t put her back into her old things.
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: Certainly. Anything you like. Is that all?
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Thank you, sir. That’s all.
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: She goes out.

You know, Pickering, that woman has the most extraordinary ideas about me. Here I am, a shy, diffident sort of man. I’ve never been able to feel really grown-up and tremendous, like other chaps. And yet she’s firmly persuaded that I’m an arbitrary overbearing bossing kind of person. I can’t account for it.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Mrs. Pearce returns.
If you please, sir, the trouble’s beginning already. There’s a dustman downstairs, Alfred Doolittle, wants to see you. He says you have his daughter here.
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: PICKERING [rising] Phew!
I say! [He retreats to the hearthrug].
HIGGINS [promptly] Send the blackguard up.
Oh, very well, sir.
units.name: MRS. PEARCE

units.text: She goes out.
He may not be a blackguard, Higgins.
units.name: PICKERING

units.text: Nonsense. Of course he’s a blackguard.
units.name: HIGGINS
